cards.heading: The ip route command
cards.body: A static route names a destination prefix and mask, then either a next-hop address or an exit interface. Next-hop routes are the usual choice on Ethernet. The route only goes into the table if the router can reach the next hop.

cards.heading: Default route
cards.body: 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 matches everything, so it catches any destination without a more specific route. Edge routers typically point a default route at the ISP.
cards.example:
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.1
Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

cards.heading: Floating static routes
cards.body: Add an administrative distance at the end of the command to make a backup route. Because its AD is higher than the primary route's, it stays out of the routing table until the primary disappears.

cards.heading: Verify with show ip route and ping
cards.body: Check that the route is installed with code S, then ping. A ping needs routes in both directions: the far end must know how to reach your source address too.

cards.heading: IPv6 static routes
cards.body: IPv6 works the same way with 'ipv6 route'. Enable routing first with 'ipv6 unicast-routing'. The default route is ::/0.
cards.example:
ipv6 unicast-routing
ipv6 route 2001:db8:3::/64 2001:db8:12::2
ipv6 route ::/0 2001:db8:12::2
